verses.1: After seventy years, it will be made holy.
verses.2: And this is what the Shmita means: No man who is under the rule of Moses may harm his neighbor or his brother. This is because Shmita is a commandment given by God.
verses.3: The foreigner will be brought before you, and your brother who becomes your enemy will be punished by your hands.
verses.4: I am sorry, for there will be no inheritance in you. For as Jehovah your God blesses you, so he also will give you the land that he has promised to give you as a inheritance.
verses.5: Only if you hear the voice of the LORD your God, and obey His commands to carry out all these laws that I am giving you today.
verses.6: For Jehovah your God will bless you as he has promised. You have conquered many nations, and you will not be conquered by them. You have ruled over many nations, and no one will be able to rule over you.
verses.7: For there may be an enemy among your own brothers, in one of your gates, in the land that Yahweh your God gives you. Do not trust your heart, and do not stretch out your hand against your brother who is your enemy.
verses.8: For when you open your hand to him, and he touches us with what is lacking in him.
verses.9: Keep this in mind, so that there will be no disagreement between your heart and your words. It is said that in the seventh year of the reign of King Hezekiah, there was a time of great suffering for you. Do not give him anything. Call upon Jehovah, and may there be no sin in you.
verses.10: Give him what he deserves. Do not worry about it in your heart. For through this act, Jehovah your God will bless you in all your endeavors and in everything you do.
verses.11: For my father will never cease to be near the earth. Therefore, I command you to say, “Open your hand and help your brothers and your poor people in your land.”
verses.12: Your Hebrew brother or sister will be sold to you. He or she will serve you for six years. In the seventh year, we will be released from your service.
verses.13: And if you send them away as strangers from your own household, do not send them away as worthless people.
verses.14: He will give him your gifts, your blessings, and everything that Jehovah your God has granted you. He will give it to him.
verses.15: And you remember that you were a slave in the land of Egypt. But Jehovah your God saved you from there. Therefore, I command you to do this today.
verses.16: And it shall be as if he said, “I will not leave your side, for I love you and your home. It is good for me to be with you.”
verses.17: And you took the rod and put it in his mouth, so that he could serve you forever. And indeed, you will do just as you said.
verses.18: It will not be difficult for you to send him away from your presence, because your servant will be paid back after six years. And Jehovah your God will bless you in all that you do.
verses.19: All the livestock that is born in your fields and in your vineyards shall be holy to your God. You shall not work with livestock from your own fields, nor shall you plow with livestock from your own vineyards.
verses.20: Before Jehovah your God, we will eat him year after year, in the place that Jehovah chooses—you and your house.
verses.21: And if there is any death or destruction in it, do not worship it as your God.
verses.22: In your gates, we will eat the dirty and the clean together, like fish and crabs.
verses.23: Only his blood shall not be eaten on the earth; it shall be poured out like water.
